analysis.title: GS Lin - Prime Perspective: AI Unwinds 15 Oct 2026
key_insights: Global equities were significantly net sold on Oct 14 (-2.1 SDs vs 1-year), driven by risk unwinds with long sales outpacing short sales about 3 to 1.

Nearly all major regions were net sold, led by North America (long-and-short sales) and EM Asia (long sales > short covers). Korea and Taiwan were the most net sold Asian markets, driven by long sales.
Foreign investors made significant net sales in both Taiwan and Korea overnight on Oct 15, based on exchange-reported data.
US equities were 66% of global net selling (-1.8 SDs vs 1-year), driven by long-and-short sales (1.9 to 1). Single stocks and macro products were both net sold, at 54%/46% of the dollar net selling.
8 of 11 US sectors were net sold, led by Info Tech and Industrials. Health Care and Staples were the most net bought, which GS reads as an incrementally defensive posture.
All US Info Tech subsectors were net sold: Software (short-and-long sales) led, then Semis & Semi Equipment (long sales), and to a lesser extent IT Services (long sales).
Global AI stocks (GSXGGLAI constituents) saw the second-largest net selling of the past year after July (-2.8 Z score), driven by long-and-short sales (3.5 to 1).
Hedge funds net sold Global AI stocks for five consecutive sessions (Oct 8-14). All of the cumulative hedge fund net buying in this group since the start of 2025 has now been reversed.

Net allocation to Global AI stocks is 26.1% of global single-stock net market value, down from a 31.7% peak in early June. It sits in the 49th percentile vs the past year and the 83rd vs the past three years.
The aggregate long/short ratio across Global AI stocks is 3.27, down from a 4.34 peak in early June. It sits in the 7th percentile vs the past year and the 64th vs the past three years.
Hedge fund net leverage fell 1.5 pts on the day and 4.3 pts MTD to 73.3%, in the 6th percentile vs the past year. Gross leverage is 310.3%, in the 91st percentile vs the past three years.
Fundamental L/S managers lost money on Oct 14 mainly from beta, with TMT L/S down the most (-2.7%). Systematic managers were up +0.5%.

Foreign net selling in Taiwan and Korea may extend the unwind in Asian technology markets.
